terms.meaning: a small class that describes the fields a request must or may contain, used to check incoming data.
a helper library that attaches checks such as must not be empty or must be a text value to fields.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for validation and docs
sections.what: Brings in the validation checks and the documentation helpers that the request classes below use.

sections.name: ConsentPurpose
sections.title: Named consent purposes
sections.what: Lists the five purposes a user can consent to: AI summarization, AI chat, data processing, family sharing and analytics.
sections.why: Likely reason: a fixed list gives the app one set of names to check against.
sections.watch_out: Nothing in the request classes below enforces this list, so a value outside it is still accepted.

sections.name: GrantConsentDto
sections.title: Grant consent request rules
sections.what: Describes the body for granting consent: a required purpose of up to 100 characters, plus an optional IP address of up to 45 characters and an optional user agent of up to 500 characters. Each field is documented for the API page.
sections.why: Likely reason: the service stores the IP address and user agent as evidence of where and how the user agreed.
sections.watch_out: These optional fields come from the caller, so they can hold any value the caller sends.

sections.name: RevokeConsentDto
sections.title: Withdraw consent request rules
sections.what: Describes the body for withdrawing consent: a required purpose of up to 100 characters.
sections.why: Likely reason: withdrawal needs only the purpose name because the user is identified from the login.
sections.watch_out: The purpose is not checked against the named list, so a misspelled name creates a separate withdrawn record and does not cancel the real consent.

summary: Defines the shape and validation rules for the grant and revoke requests in the consent feature, and lists the named consent purposes.
purpose: Makes sure consent requests include a purpose name and stay within length limits, and documents each field for the API page.
why: Likely reason: checking input at the edge keeps bad data out of the database. The reason for the exact limits is not stated in the code.
how: 1) Define the list of named purposes. 2) Define the grant request with a required purpose of up to 100 characters, and optional IP address and user agent fields with length limits. 3) Define the revoke request with only the purpose field. 4) Validation checks run when a request arrives, and the API documentation is produced from the same descriptions.
inputs: JSON request bodies sent by the app or another client.
outputs: Checked request objects for the consent service, or a validation error that the framework returns to the caller.
risks: The purpose field accepts any text up to 100 characters and the named list is not used to check it, so unknown purposes get stored. The IP address field allows 45 characters, which fits IPv6 addresses, but the value is not checked to be a real address. The named list here can drift from the purposes checked elsewhere in the app.
debug: If a consent request is rejected, read the validation message returned to the caller. If an unknown purpose was saved, compare the value sent with the named purpose list. Check the API documentation page for the description of each field.
